prs.title: Use supported MicroBuild source-analysis pool
prs.author: joj
prs.body:
Updates `sdl.sourceAnalysisPool` in `tools/pipelines/typescript-build.yml`
from `VSEngSS-MicroBuild2022-1ES` to `VSEng-MicroBuildVSStable`.

The Linux build pool (`AzurePipelines-EO` / `1ESPT-Ubuntu22.04`) and all build,
signing, and publishing steps remain unchanged.

Also migrates the source-analysis pools in:
- `tools/pipelines/typescript-publish.yml`
- `tools/pipelines/vscode-typescript-build.yml`
- `tools/pipelines/vscode-typescript-publish.yml`

Each additional file changes only `sdl.sourceAnalysisPool`; Linux execution pools
and build/publish/signing behavior remain unchanged.

prs.title: [api] Client performance optimizations
prs.author: andrewbranch
prs.body:
Six independent changes, best viewed one commit at a time.

This reduces wall clock time for the recommended ruleset over 1024 files in https://github.com/typescript-eslint/performance by 5.8% on my machine, with 57% fewer allocations from the client. Retained heap falls by 2.4%. Most of the allocation reduction is from 47fddf52d09cdca019d389571e006062729c19f2.

The batched `getSymbolAtLocation` benchmark from our own suite is also 28% faster in the async client and 22% faster in the sync client.

prs.title: Make LSP server load content mappers only from node_modules inside workspace folders
prs.author: andrewbranch
prs.body: When you open a file from an _untrusted directory_ into a _trusted_ VS Code window, VS Code asks you if you really want to do that. But that warning can be permanently suppressed, and users might find it surprising that by trusting the file, TypeScript's language server will find its tsconfig and potentially load content mappers that it resolves from the node_modules belonging to that untrusted directory. This PR prevents that by only allowing the LSP server to load content mappers resolved to a node_modules directory contained by an open workspace folder.

prs.title: [api] Remove package.json "imports"
prs.author: andrewbranch
prs.body:
This is a prerequisite to being able to load the API directly from a CDN, prior to #63858

Basically, we're in a pick-any-three situation between

1. Run tests from TS source in plain Node.js without a build or loader
2. Use real TS enums for type checking
3. Be able to load directly from a CDN
4. ~~Produce the output JS entirely with `tsc`~~ Put the enums in `src` and produce output to `dist` entirely with `tsc`

In this PR, we are gaining (3) and losing (4); ~~we now need to copy `.js` and `.d.ts` files from `src` to `dist` as part of the API build~~ we now just generate the built enums to a top-level `enums` directory that gets included in the packed package, similar to `vendor`.
